---
title: "Post-aggregation analysis"
output: html_document
params:
  transcript_filter: "biotype_filtered"
---

```{r, load-data}
set.seed(getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_SEED", 42L))

keep_rows_manual <- readRDS("processed_data/keep_rows_manual.rds")
file_metadata <- fread("processed_data/file_table.csv.gz")
metadata <- fread(sample_metadata_file)
event_annotations_dt <- fread("processed_data/event_annotations_dt.csv.gz")
psi_long_dt <- fread("processed_data/psi_long_dt.csv.gz")
ijc_sjc_dt <- fread("processed_data/ijc_sjc_dt.csv.gz")
# locate
file_metadata[,
  local_file := file.path(sample_dt_dir, paste0(basename(file_path), ".tab.gz"))
]
stopifnot(file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq", all(file.exists(local_file))])

# # we only need ChIP-Seq data, since WGBS has been aggregated via the matrices
# file_table <- file_table[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq"]

# load WGBS data
wgbs_agg <- fread(file.path(sample_dt_dir, "WGBS_agg.csv.gz"))
wgbs_agg <- wgbs_agg[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]
wgbs_agg <- melt(
  wgbs_agg,
  id.vars = c("ID", "ihec", "name"),
  value.name = "score",
  variable.name = "experiment_type",
  measure.vars = c("score", "n")
)
wgbs_agg[experiment_type == "score", experiment_type := "DNAm"]
wgbs_agg[experiment_type == "n", experiment_type := "CpGs"]

wgbs_agg[, ihec := sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", ihec)]

# bind all the samples for the histone marks
#
# Memory note: at full scale this table is ~1.03e9 rows (2430 files x
# ~424k windows), so column choices matter a lot here. bigWigAverageOverBed
# emits 8 columns (name size covered sum mean0 mean min max); only `name`
# (window id) and `mean` are ever used downstream (everything else is
# discarded before the dcast a few lines below and nothing later re-reads
# it) — keeping all 8 would cost ~40 bytes/row x 1.03e9 rows =~ 41 GB for
# columns that are immediately dropped. `select=` at fread() time avoids
# ever allocating them. Likewise, attaching `ihec`/`experiment_type` per
# file here (instead of carrying the full `local_file` path column through
# the whole long table, as before) saves another ~8 GB of pure pointer
# overhead for a value only ever used to look these two up.
chip_files <- file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq"]
histone_dt <- rbindlist(
  pbmcapply::pbmcmapply(
    FUN = function(file, this_ihec, this_mark) {
      dt <- fread(file, select = c(1, 6), col.names = c("name", "score"))
      dt <- dt[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]
      dt[, ihec := this_ihec]
      dt[, experiment_type := this_mark]
      dt
    },
    file = chip_files$local_file,
    this_ihec = chip_files$epirr_id_without_version,
    this_mark = chip_files$experiment_type,
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE
  )
)

# find common cols and rows
common_ihec <- intersect(histone_dt[, unique(ihec)], wgbs_agg[, unique(ihec)])
common_cols <- intersect(names(histone_dt), names(wgbs_agg))
```


```{r, build-aggregated-dt}
# bind histone and WGBS data
aggregated_dt <- rbindlist(list(
  histone_dt[ihec %in% common_ihec, ..common_cols],
  wgbs_agg[ihec %in% common_ihec, ..common_cols]
))

# some data wrangling to prepare the data for putting into wide format
aggregated_dt[, c("position", "ID") := tstrsplit(name, "_", fixed = TRUE)]
# there is an ID for all of them, so remove this line
# aggregated_dt[is.na(ID), c("position", "ID"):=list('event_name', position)]
# aggregated_dt[position=="up", position:="upstream_other_region"]
# aggregated_dt[position=="down", position:="downstream_other_region"]
aggregated_dt[, experiment_type := droplevels(experiment_type)]
aggregated_dt[, ihec := as.factor(ihec)]
aggregated_dt[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
# from long to wide
aggregated_dt <- dcast(
  aggregated_dt,
  ihec + ID ~ experiment_type + position,
  value.var = "score",
  sep = ";"
)
setnames(aggregated_dt, old = "ihec", new = "IHEC")

# §4.13l — per-mark observed/imputed source covariate. 04-2-chip-signal-sanity
# found imputed ChIP tracks run 1.7-7x higher median signal than observed for
# every mark (worst for H3K27me3/H3K9me3), and this status is per (sample,
# mark) — a sample can have some marks observed and others imputed — so it
# is NOT captured by anything already in aggregated_dt. Derived directly
# from chip_files (a per-file property, constant across all windows for a
# mark) rather than carried through the window-level table.
#
# Written as a STRING ("observed"/"imputed"), not a 0/1 flag, so it is
# auto-routed to the categorical/nominal branch of both downstream
# pipelines without any code changes there: splicing_ml's
# infer_feature_columns() buckets by dtype (non-numeric -> categorical_cols
# -> OneHotEncoder, same as `protocol`); 07-ml-event-glmnet-tidymodels.R's
# tidymodels recipe uses all_nominal_predictors() -> step_dummy(). A numeric
# 0/1 encoding would risk being misclassified as a continuous histone
# signal by splicing_ml's `col.startswith("H3K")` clip-column rule if named
# with an H3K prefix; the `_source` suffix and string dtype sidestep this
# even though the column also happens to start with "H3K".
chip_source <- unique(chip_files[, .(
  IHEC = epirr_id_without_version,
  mark = experiment_type,
  source = fifelse(uuid == "imputed", "imputed", "observed")
)])
chip_source_wide <- dcast(chip_source, IHEC ~ mark, value.var = "source")
source_cols <- setdiff(names(chip_source_wide), "IHEC")
setnames(
  chip_source_wide,
  old = source_cols,
  new = paste0(source_cols, "_source")
)
source_cols <- paste0(source_cols, "_source")

aggregated_dt[
  chip_source_wide,
  on = "IHEC",
  (source_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", source_cols))
]

# write full table to disk
fwrite(aggregated_dt, "processed_data/aggregated_dt.csv.gz")
```


```{r, chip-signal-sanity}
# §4.13b — ChIP signal assertion: NA fraction < 5% and non-negative, for
# observed (non-imputed) samples only. Imputed samples may have higher NA.
observed_ihec <- file_metadata[
  assay_type == "ChIP-Seq" & uuid != "imputed",
  unique(epirr_id_without_version)
]
chip_marks <- file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq", unique(experiment_type)]
chip_cols <- grep(
  paste0("^(", paste(chip_marks, collapse = "|"), ");"),
  names(aggregated_dt),
  value = TRUE
)
observed_dt <- aggregated_dt[IHEC %in% observed_ihec]
for (col in chip_cols) {
  vals <- observed_dt[[col]]
  na_frac <- mean(is.na(vals))
  stopifnot(na_frac < 0.05)
  stopifnot(all(vals[!is.na(vals)] >= 0))
}
```


```{r, melt-psi}
# psi_long_dt from 03 is already long format (ID, uuid, psi) — no melt needed
melted_psi <- copy(psi_long_dt)
setnames(melted_psi, "psi", "PSI")
melted_psi[
  event_annotations_dt,
  on = .(ID),
  c("Event Type", "transcript_filter", "gene_id") := .(
    `Event Type`,
    transcript_filter,
    gene_id
  )
]
melted_psi <- melted_psi[!is.na(PSI)]
melted_psi[file_metadata, on = .(uuid), IHEC := epirr_id_without_version]
```


```{r, expand-aggregated-dt}
# guard against re-running this chunk on an already-expanded aggregated_dt
# (merge() would silently produce PSI.x/PSI.y instead of erroring clearly).
# If this trips, reload the cheap checkpoint instead of rerunning
# build-aggregated-dt: aggregated_dt <- fread("processed_data/aggregated_dt.csv.gz")
stopifnot(!("PSI" %in% names(aggregated_dt)))

# merge PSI on the aggregated table
aggregated_dt <- merge(
  aggregated_dt,
  melted_psi[
    ID %in% keep_rows_manual & !is.na(PSI),
    .(ID, IHEC, uuid, PSI, transcript_filter)
  ],
  by = c("ID", "IHEC")
)
# remove NA PSIs
aggregated_dt <- aggregated_dt[!is.na(PSI)]

# §4.8 — carry junction read counts (IJC/SJC) forward from 03. Needed
# downstream for coverage-weighted model fitting (sample_weight = IJC + SJC)
# and beta-binomial regression on raw counts, and here for the §4.13i
# coverage sanity check. Joined on (ID, uuid) — same keys as psi_long_dt.
aggregated_dt[
  ijc_sjc_dt,
  on = .(ID, uuid),
  c("IJC", "SJC") := .(i.IJC, i.SJC)
]

# NA for columns starting with CpGs can be replaced by 0, because NA means no CpGs were covered in that window, which is equivalent to 0.
for (i in grep("^CpGs", names(aggregated_dt))) {
  set(aggregated_dt, i = which(is.na(aggregated_dt[[i]])), j = i, value = 0)
}

# gather the intrinsic features
# Note: splice-site scores (3ss, 5ss, etc.) joined separately after MaxEntScan rule
cols_to_add <- c(
  "distance_TSS",
  "distance_TES",
  "distance_gene_start",
  "distance_gene_end",
  "width;upstream_other_region",
  "width;event_name",
  "width;downstream_other_region",
  "Event Type",
  "gene_id",
  "seqnames",
  "Variability"
)

# add the intrinsic features
aggregated_dt[
  event_annotations_dt,
  on = .(ID),
  (cols_to_add) := mget(cols_to_add)
]
# also add the protocol
aggregated_dt[file_metadata, on = .(uuid), protocol := experiment_type]
# add the ontology term and the project
aggregated_dt[
  metadata,
  on = c(IHEC = "epirr_id_without_version"),
  c("ontology", "project") := .(
    factor(harmonized_sample_ontology_term_high_order_fig1),
    factor(project)
  )
]

# §2.1 — QC flag count covariate, joined by uuid (NOT epirr_id_without_version:
# epirrs with both mRNA-Seq + total-RNA-Seq have multiple uuids). No samples
# dropped; all 405 epirrs retained.
qc_flag_covariates <- fread("processed_data/qc_flag_covariates.csv")
aggregated_dt[
  qc_flag_covariates,
  on = .(uuid),
  qc_flag_count := i.qc_flag_count
]


# load transcript ids per filter
filtered_transcript_ids <- readRDS(
  "splicing_analysis/filtered_transcript_ids.rds"
)
# `transcript_filters` was previously an undefined variable here (only
# worked by accident if a prior interactive session had it in the global
# env, e.g. from running 03 first) — derive it from the actual upstream
# artifact instead of hardcoding a second copy of the three filter names.
transcript_filters <- names(filtered_transcript_ids)

### Old implementation recomputed TPM, now that we have §4.12b, we use the lengthScaledTPM + vst from 04-5-rnaseq-normalisation.Rmd
# # load isoform quantifications
# isoform_quants <- fread(
#   "splicing_analysis/isoform_quantifications_subset.tsv.gz"
# )
# # compute gene-level quantifications
# gene_quants <- rbindlist(
#   sapply(
#     transcript_filters,
#     function(this_transcript_filter) {
#       # subset the isoform quantifications to the samples we want to use
#       this_filtered_transcripts <- filtered_transcript_ids[[
#         this_transcript_filter
#       ]]

#       # filter the isoform quantifications to the filtered transcripts and compute gene-level quantifications by summing the TPMs of the transcripts per gene
#       isoform_quants_filtered <- copy(isoform_quants[
#         transcript_id %in% this_filtered_transcripts
#       ])
#       isoform_quants_filtered[
#         effective_length > 0,
#         RPK := 1000 * expected_count / effective_length,
#         by = .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[,
#         TPM_rec := 1000000 * RPK / sum(RPK, na.rm = TRUE),
#         by = .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[is.na(TPM_rec), TPM_rec := 0]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[,
#         TPM_scale := 1000000 * TPM / sum(TPM, na.rm = TRUE),
#         .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#     },
#     simplify = FALSE
#   ),
#   idcol = "transcript_filter"
# )
# # manually change gene_id for ENSG00000213593.9_and_ENSG00000254462.1_and_ENSG00000211450.9_and_ENSG00000198561.13 from the manual ids that were kept
# # aggregated_dt[gene_id == "ENSG00000213593.9_and_ENSG00000254462.1_and_ENSG00000211450.9_and_ENSG00000198561.13", gene_id := "ENSG00000198561.13"]
# # §4.12a — gene_quants is at transcript level (one row per transcript per
# # sample); aggregate to gene level before joining, otherwise data.table's
# # last-write-wins `:=` join picks an arbitrary single transcript's TPM_scale
# # instead of the gene-level sum across all transcripts.
# gene_quants_agg <- gene_quants[,
#   .(gene_expression = sum(TPM_scale, na.rm = TRUE)),
#   by = .(transcript_filter, uuid, gene_id)
# ]

gene_quants_agg <- fread("processed_data/gene_expression_normalised.csv.gz")

# §4.12b — keep BOTH normalised representations under explicit names; there
# is deliberately no ambiguous `gene_expression` column. Consumers pick by
# column structure (see revision/PLAN.md §4.12b, file-changes specs):
#   - gene_expression_getmm : GeTMM-CPM, length- AND composition-corrected,
#     cross-gene comparable WITHOUT per-gene z-scoring. Use where the feature
#     is one column with many different host genes stacked in the rows and no
#     per-gene rescaling happens -> the genome-wide pooled table
#     (splicing_ml). Also the correct scale for any raw >=0 / log1p / ==0 /
#     threshold check (the §4.12e mask uses it below).
#   - gene_expression_vst : DESeq2 vst, variance-stabilised, cross-SAMPLE
#     comparable only (NOT length-corrected). Use where each column is a
#     single gene varying across samples and gets z-scored per column anyway
#     -> event-specific models (07/09) and every RBP expression column.
#     Roughly log2-scale, CAN BE NEGATIVE: never apply log1p/log to it.
aggregated_dt[
  gene_quants_agg,
  on = .(transcript_filter, uuid, gene_id),
  c("gene_expression_vst", "gene_expression_getmm") := .(
    i.gene_expression_vst,
    i.gene_expression_getmm
  )
]

# §4.12e — decision check: do AS-event-hosting genes even need a
# low-expression filter, or are they already pre-selected for expression by
# rMATS (an event needs junction reads spanning it to be called at all)?
# Compares the per-gene expression distribution of AS-event genes against
# ALL annotation-passing genes (the same universe gene_quants_agg is built
# from, genome-wide -- see 02-SUPPA2-analysis.Rmd filter-annotation chunk --
# NOT restricted to AS events). Classic genome-wide expression is bimodal
# (on/off: housekeeping/expressed vs silenced genes); if AS-event genes are
# already unimodal and clear of the low mode, masking low-expression rows
# below is redundant and can be dropped.
#
# Granularity: one point per (gene_id, transcript_filter), median expression
# across samples -- the natural granularity for "is this gene on or off",
# as opposed to the per-(gene,sample) granularity the old masking applied.
# Checked on BOTH representations: gene_expression_getmm (CPM-like, >= 0,
# what the old threshold was meant for) and gene_expression_vst (the actual
# feature fed to models -- variance-stabilised, roughly log2-scale, can be
# negative, so it gets no log1p and no comparable raw threshold line).
min_gene_expression <- getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_MIN_GENE_EXPRESSION", 1)

event_genes <- unique(event_annotations_dt[, .(transcript_filter, gene_id)])
event_genes[, gene_id := gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id)]

gene_median_expr <- gene_quants_agg[,
  .(
    median_getmm = median(gene_expression_getmm, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_vst = median(gene_expression_vst, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  by = .(transcript_filter, gene_id)
]
gene_median_expr[, gene_id_stripped := gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id)]
gene_median_expr[,
  group := fifelse(
    paste(transcript_filter, gene_id_stripped) %in%
      event_genes[, paste(transcript_filter, gene_id)],
    "AS-event gene",
    "background (all genes)"
  )
]

dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# shared plot + Hartigan dip test (unimodality) logic for a given
# representation column -- same dip test already used in
# 03-prepare-aggregation.Rmd for variability measures. p > 0.05 -> can't
# reject unimodal null; p < 0.05 -> bimodal signal.
run_need_filter_check <- function(
  value_col,
  x_expr,
  x_lab,
  vline_val,
  out_suffix
) {
  plot_dt <- copy(gene_median_expr)
  plot_dt[, x_val := x_expr(get(value_col))]

  p <- ggplot(plot_dt, aes(x = x_val, fill = group, color = group)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
    facet_wrap(~transcript_filter, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(
      title = sprintf(
        "per-gene median %s: AS-event genes vs all genes",
        value_col
      ),
      x = x_lab
    )
  if (!is.null(vline_val)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(xintercept = vline_val, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
      labs(subtitle = "dashed line = former §4.12e masking threshold")
  }
  print(p)
  ggsave(
    sprintf("qc/distributions/gene_expression_need_filter_check_%s.pdf", out_suffix),
    p,
    width = 8,
    height = 3 * length(transcript_filters)
  )

  if (requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) {
    dip_results <- plot_dt[,
      {
        d <- diptest::dip.test(x_val)
        list(dip_statistic = unname(d$statistic), p_value = d$p.value, n = .N)
      },
      by = .(transcript_filter, group)
    ]
    print(dip_results)
    fwrite(
      dip_results,
      sprintf("qc/gene_expression_need_filter_dip_test_%s.csv", out_suffix)
    )
  } else {
    warning("diptest package not available; skipping bimodality dip test")
  }
}

run_need_filter_check(
  value_col = "median_getmm",
  x_expr = log1p,
  x_lab = "log1p(median gene_expression_getmm)",
  vline_val = log1p(min_gene_expression),
  out_suffix = "getmm"
)
run_need_filter_check(
  value_col = "median_vst",
  x_expr = identity,
  x_lab = "median gene_expression_vst",
  vline_val = NULL,
  out_suffix = "vst"
)

min_samples_per_event <- getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_MIN_SAMPLES_PER_EVENT", 10)

# --- coverage-vs-expression overlap check --------------------------------
# IJC/SJC (junction-read sample weighting, §4.8) already down-weights noisy
# low-coverage rows in the loss. If gene_expression_getmm is highly
# correlated with junction coverage, expression masking would be largely
# redundant with that weighting; if the correlation is weak, the two catch
# different noise sources (whole-gene expression vs event-specific junction
# reads) and masking adds something coverage-weighting doesn't.
coverage_expr_cor <- aggregated_dt[,
  {
    keep <- !is.na(gene_expression_getmm) & !is.na(IJC) & !is.na(SJC)
    list(
      spearman_r = cor(
        log1p(gene_expression_getmm[keep]),
        log1p(IJC[keep] + SJC[keep]),
        method = "spearman"
      ),
      n = sum(keep)
    )
  },
  by = transcript_filter
]
print(coverage_expr_cor)
fwrite(coverage_expr_cor, "qc/gene_expression_vs_junction_coverage_cor.csv")

# --- masking impact check (simulated, not applied) -----------------------
# how many events (ID x transcript_filter) would drop below
# min_samples_per_event if the §4.12e low-expression mask were applied --
# quantifies data loss before committing to the mask.
event_mask_impact <- aggregated_dt[,
  .(
    n_samples = .N,
    n_after_mask = sum(gene_expression_getmm >= min_gene_expression, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  by = .(ID, transcript_filter, `Event Type`)
]
event_mask_impact[, would_drop := n_after_mask < min_samples_per_event]

masking_impact_summary <- event_mask_impact[,
  .(
    n_events = .N,
    n_events_would_drop = sum(would_drop),
    frac_events_would_drop = mean(would_drop)
  ),
  by = .(transcript_filter, `Event Type`)
]
print(masking_impact_summary)
fwrite(masking_impact_summary, "qc/gene_expression_masking_impact.csv")

row_mask_frac <- aggregated_dt[,
  .(frac_rows_would_mask = mean(gene_expression_getmm < min_gene_expression, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = transcript_filter
]
print(row_mask_frac)
fwrite(row_mask_frac, "qc/gene_expression_masking_row_frac.csv")

# Decision: KEEP masking. Evidence from the checks above:
#  - dip test: AS-event genes are MORE bimodal than the genome-wide
#    background (e.g. biotype_filtered getmm: dip=0.050 p<0.001 for event
#    genes vs dip=0.0085 for background) -- a real low-expression
#    subpopulation survives among event-hosting genes, contrary to the
#    "already pre-selected for expression by rMATS" hypothesis.
#  - coverage overlap: spearman r(gene_expression_getmm, IJC+SJC) ~ 0.70-0.72
#    across filters -- correlated with junction-read sample weighting
#    (§4.8) but far from redundant (30%+ unexplained variance), so masking
#    catches noise the coverage weighting doesn't.
#  - impact: cheap to apply -- only 8.5-12.8% of (event, sample) rows get
#    masked, and only 0.3-1.9% of events are lost entirely to the
#    min_samples_per_event floor below.
# PSI in the masked (low-expression) rows is a noisy estimate (few
# informative reads to derive inclusion/skip ratio from), so mask it to NA
# rather than trusting it. Masking (not dropping the row outright) lets the
# sample-count check below decide per-event whether enough non-masked
# samples remain to keep modelling the event at all.
#
# Threshold is checked against gene_expression_getmm (CPM-like, >= 0, same
# convention as the old TPM>=1 cutoff), NOT gene_expression (vst): vst is
# variance-stabilised, roughly log2-scale, and can be negative, so
# comparing it to a raw threshold of 1 doesn't correspond to "low
# expression".
aggregated_dt[gene_expression_getmm < min_gene_expression, PSI := NA]

event_sample_counts <- aggregated_dt[
  !is.na(PSI),
  .N,
  by = .(ID, transcript_filter)
]
low_sample_events <- event_sample_counts[
  N < min_samples_per_event,
  .(ID, transcript_filter)
]
if (nrow(low_sample_events) > 0) {
  aggregated_dt <- aggregated_dt[
    !low_sample_events,
    on = .(ID, transcript_filter)
  ]
}
# drop rows masked to NA above (and any events removed entirely by the
# sample-count check, which have no remaining non-NA rows anyway)
aggregated_dt <- aggregated_dt[!is.na(PSI)]

# make sure all of the gene_expression values are at least one: (deprecated because we don't have the suppa tpm filter anymore)
# stopifnot(all(aggregated_dt[, gene_expression >= 1]))
# log the expression, we do that later
# aggregated_dt[, gene_expression := log2(gene_expression)]

# remove the gene_id version
aggregated_dt[, gene_id := gsub(pattern = ".\\d+$", "", gene_id)]

# max promoter and summed enhancer are not used anymore
# # get the epirrs for which there is observed H3K27ac because only they have max_promoter and summed_enhancer
# ihec_of_interest <- file_metadata[experiment_type == "H3K27ac" & uuid != "imputed", .(IHEC = epirr_id_without_version, uuid)]

# # read the max promoter
# max_promoter <- fread("data/GeneMaxPromoterSignal.txt.gz") # from /IHEC/post_processed_data/Analysis/IHEC_gABC_Interactions/GeneMaxPromoterSignal.txt.gz
# promoter_melt <- melt(max_promoter, id.vars = "Ensembl ID", variable.name = "uuid", value.name = "max_promoter", variable.factor = FALSE)
# promoter_merged <- promoter_melt[ihec_of_interest, on = .(uuid)][, .(IHEC, uuid, gene_id = `Ensembl ID`, max_promoter)]

# # read the summed enhancer
```

```{r, gene-expression-sanity}
# §4.13d — gene expression distribution sanity (post §4.12a fix)
sanity_csv <- "qc/sanity_summary.csv"
append_sanity <- function(check_name, status, value, threshold, notes = "") {
  fwrite(
    data.table(
      check_name = check_name,
      status = status,
      value = value,
      threshold = threshold,
      notes = notes
    ),
    sanity_csv,
    append = TRUE
  )
}

dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 1. log1p(gene_expression_getmm) boxplot by protocol
# getmm (CPM-like, >= 0) is the log1p-safe representation; vst can be
# negative and would produce NaNs under log().
p_gene_expr <- ggplot(
  unique(aggregated_dt[, .(uuid, protocol, gene_expression_getmm)]),
  aes(x = protocol, y = log1p(gene_expression_getmm))
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "log1p(gene_expression_getmm) by protocol",
    x = "protocol",
    y = "log1p(gene_expression_getmm)"
  )
print(p_gene_expr)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/gene_expression_by_protocol.pdf",
  p_gene_expr,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)

# 2. rank correlation across transcript_filter levels (getmm = expression
# level; the §4.12a bug check)
expr_by_filter <- unique(aggregated_dt[, .(
  uuid,
  gene_id,
  transcript_filter,
  gene_expression_getmm
)])
expr_wide <- dcast(
  expr_by_filter,
  uuid + gene_id ~ transcript_filter,
  value.var = "gene_expression_getmm"
)
filter_cols <- setdiff(names(expr_wide), c("uuid", "gene_id"))
if (length(filter_cols) >= 2) {
  rank_cor <- cor(
    expr_wide[[filter_cols[1]]],
    expr_wide[[filter_cols[2]]],
    method = "spearman",
    use = "complete.obs"
  )
  append_sanity(
    "gene_expression_rank_cor_across_filters",
    ifelse(rank_cor > 0.95, "PASS", "WARN"),
    rank_cor,
    0.95,
    "if < 0.5, §4.12a bug still active"
  )
}

# 3. % zero-expression events per sample (getmm: CPM-like, can be exactly 0;
# vst never is, so == 0 is only meaningful on getmm)
zero_frac_by_sample <- aggregated_dt[,
  .(zero_frac = mean(gene_expression_getmm == 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = uuid
]
pct_over_thresh <- zero_frac_by_sample[, mean(zero_frac >= 0.30)]
append_sanity(
  "gene_expression_zero_frac_per_sample",
  ifelse(pct_over_thresh < 0.30, "PASS", "WARN"),
  pct_over_thresh,
  0.30,
  "fraction of samples with >=30% zero-expression events"
)

# 4. §4.12e post-mask verification -- confirms no row with
# gene_expression_getmm below threshold survived masking (catches join/unit
# mistakes like the previous vst-vs-getmm mismatch), and logs how many
# events (ID x transcript_filter) were dropped entirely because
# low-expression masking left them under min_samples_per_event. Compare
# against the pre-mask simulated estimate in
# qc/gene_expression_masking_impact.csv (should match).
stopifnot(all(aggregated_dt$gene_expression_getmm >= min_gene_expression))
append_sanity(
  "gene_expression_getmm_below_threshold_postmask",
  "PASS",
  0,
  min_gene_expression,
  "rows remaining below masking threshold after §4.12e (should always be 0; assertion above enforces it)"
)

n_events_dropped_low_expr <- low_sample_events[, uniqueN(paste(
  ID,
  transcript_filter
))]
append_sanity(
  "gene_expression_events_dropped_low_expression",
  "INFO",
  n_events_dropped_low_expr,
  min_samples_per_event,
  "events (ID x transcript_filter) dropped after low-expression masking left < min_samples_per_event non-NA samples"
)
```


```{r, junction-coverage-sanity}
# §4.13i — junction read coverage sanity. Complements §4.8: verifies the
# IJC/SJC counts just joined in are high enough that PSI is a trustworthy
# ratio rather than noise from a handful of reads.
bf_dt <- aggregated_dt[transcript_filter == "biotype_filtered"]

p_junction_cov <- ggplot(bf_dt, aes(x = log10(IJC + SJC + 1))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~`Event Type`, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "log10(IJC + SJC + 1), biotype_filtered",
    x = "log10(IJC + SJC + 1)"
  )
print(p_junction_cov)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/junction_coverage.pdf",
  p_junction_cov,
  width = 9,
  height = 5
)

# Conditional median (across expressing samples only, IJC+SJC > 0) per
# event. Zeros excluded: IJC = SJC = 0 means rMATS reported PSI = NA for
# that sample (unexpressed), not a low-coverage quantification — including
# them would understate coverage for tissue-specific events that are
# unexpressed in most samples but well-covered where they are expressed.
event_coverage <- bf_dt[
  IJC + SJC > 0,
  .(median_coverage = median(as.double(IJC + SJC))),
  by = ID
]
frac_below_10 <- event_coverage[, mean(median_coverage < 10)]
append_sanity(
  "junction_coverage_median",
  ifelse(frac_below_10 <= 0.10, "PASS", "WARN"),
  frac_below_10,
  0.10,
  "fraction of biotype_filtered events with conditional median IJC+SJC < 10"
)
```


```{r, ri-protocol-sanity}
# §4.13k — check that the known RI PSI~protocol bias (total-RNA-Seq
# inflates RI PSI by ~0.05 vs mRNA-Seq) isn't concentrated in specific
# ontologies. An ontology sampled almost entirely by one protocol would let
# protocol bias masquerade as a genuine tissue effect downstream, since
# protocol and ontology become statistically inseparable in that subgroup.
#
# Two things actually need showing here, and neither is "residuals from
# lm(PSI~protocol)" (tried first, dropped): that shows leftover PSI
# variance with the protocol effect removed, which is bounded/skewed and
# not what a confound check needs to see.
#  1. sample composition per ontology (the confound itself: is one protocol
#     dominant?) - what protocol_balance below already computes, now
#     visualized instead of hiding in a CSV row.
#  2. the protocol effect size per ontology (does the known ~0.05 bias hold
#     everywhere, or blow up in specific tissues?) - a quantity the old
#     residual plot never showed at all, since it subtracted the effect out
#     before plotting.
ri_dt_all <- rbindlist(lapply(transcript_filters, function(tf) {
  aggregated_dt[transcript_filter == tf & `Event Type` == "RI"]
}))

# --- 1. protocol composition per ontology ---------------------------------
protocol_composition <- unique(
  ri_dt_all[, .(uuid, ontology, protocol, transcript_filter)]
)[, .N, by = .(transcript_filter, ontology, protocol)]

p_protocol_composition <- ggplot(
  protocol_composition,
  aes(x = ontology, y = N, fill = protocol)
) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~transcript_filter, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "RNA-Seq protocol composition by ontology",
    x = "ontology",
    y = "fraction of samples"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
print(p_protocol_composition)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/protocol_composition_by_ontology.pdf",
  p_protocol_composition,
  width = 9,
  height = 5 * length(transcript_filters)
)

# --- 2. protocol effect size (total-RNA-Seq - mRNA-Seq) per ontology ------
# single-protocol ontologies (no contrast to estimate) get NA_real_ here and
# are still caught by the composition plot/confounded_ontologies check
# below - keep type consistent (NA_real_, not NA) so this doesn't hit the
# same integer/double by-group mismatch as the median() fix above.
protocol_effect <- ri_dt_all[,
  {
    if (uniqueN(protocol) < 2) {
      list(
        effect = NA_real_,
        ci_lo = NA_real_,
        ci_hi = NA_real_,
        n_samples = uniqueN(uuid)
      )
    } else {
      psi_total <- PSI[protocol == "total-RNA-Seq"]
      psi_mrna <- PSI[protocol == "mRNA-Seq"]
      effect <- mean(psi_total) - mean(psi_mrna)
      se <- sqrt(
        var(psi_total) / length(psi_total) + var(psi_mrna) / length(psi_mrna)
      )
      list(
        effect = effect,
        ci_lo = effect - 1.96 * se,
        ci_hi = effect + 1.96 * se,
        n_samples = uniqueN(uuid)
      )
    }
  },
  by = .(transcript_filter, ontology)
]

p_protocol_effect <- ggplot(
  protocol_effect,
  aes(
    x = ontology,
    y = effect,
    ymin = ci_lo,
    ymax = ci_hi,
    color = transcript_filter
  )
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  labs(
    title = "RI PSI protocol effect (total-RNA-Seq - mRNA-Seq) by ontology",
    subtitle = "dashed red line = known global bias (~0.05)",
    x = "ontology",
    y = "mean PSI difference",
    color = "transcript_filter"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
print(p_protocol_effect)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/ri_protocol_effect_by_ontology.pdf",
  p_protocol_effect,
  width = 9,
  height = 5
)

# flag ontologies where one protocol accounts for > 50% of samples (among
# ontologies with > 50 samples total, per spec) — below that size a
# single-protocol skew is expected sampling noise, not a real confound
for (tf in transcript_filters) {
  protocol_balance <- protocol_composition[
    transcript_filter == tf,
    .(max_frac = max(N) / sum(N), n_samples = sum(N)),
    by = ontology
  ]
  confounded_ontologies <- protocol_balance[
    max_frac > 0.5 & n_samples > 50,
    ontology
  ]
  append_sanity(
    sprintf("ri_protocol_ontology_confound_%s", tf),
    ifelse(length(confounded_ontologies) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
    length(confounded_ontologies),
    0,
    paste(
      "confounded ontologies:",
      paste(confounded_ontologies, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}
```


```{r, join-maxentscan}
# §4.13e — MaxEntScan splice-site scores (written by maxentscan_scores rule).
# Score files are row-order-aligned with their source FASTA; IDs come from
# the FASTA headers (">ID").
scores3 <- fread("processed_data/3scores.txt", col.names = c("sequence", "3ss"))
scores3down <- fread(
  "processed_data/3down_scores.txt",
  col.names = c("sequence", "3ssdown")
)
scores5 <- fread("processed_data/5scores.txt", col.names = c("sequence", "5ss"))
scores5up <- fread(
  "processed_data/5up_scores.txt",
  col.names = c("sequence", "5ssup")
)

scores3[,
  ID := as.integer(substr(
    grep("^>", readLines("processed_data/3ss.fasta"), value = TRUE),
    2,
    .Machine$integer.max
  ))
]
scores5[,
  ID := as.integer(substr(
    grep("^>", readLines("processed_data/5ss.fasta"), value = TRUE),
    2,
    .Machine$integer.max
  ))
]
scores3[, `3ssdown` := scores3down[["3ssdown"]]]
scores5[, `5ssup` := scores5up[["5ssup"]]]
scores3[, sequence := NULL]
scores5[, sequence := NULL]
ss_dt <- merge(scores3, scores5, by = "ID", all = TRUE)

ss_cols <- c("3ss", "3ssdown", "5ss", "5ssup")
aggregated_dt[ss_dt, on = .(ID), (ss_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", ss_cols))]

# sanity: distributions + NA fraction
dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ss_cols <- c("3ss", "3ssdown", "5ss", "5ssup")
# scores are per-event (constant across all sample rows sharing an ID), so
# dedupe on (ID, transcript_filter) before plotting - otherwise the
# histogram would be weighted by per-event sample count rather than by
# event, and that weighting differs across transcript_filter/Event Type.
ss_plot_cols <- c("ID", ss_cols, "Event Type", "transcript_filter")
ss_dedup <- unique(
  aggregated_dt[, ..ss_plot_cols],
  by = c("ID", "transcript_filter")
)
ss_long <- melt(
  ss_dedup,
  id.vars = c("Event Type", "transcript_filter"),
  measure.vars = ss_cols,
  variable.name = "site",
  value.name = "score"
)
p_splice_scores <- ggplot(ss_long, aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_grid(transcript_filter + `Event Type` ~ site, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "MaxEntScan score distributions", x = "score")
print(p_splice_scores)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/splice_site_scores.pdf",
  p_splice_scores,
  width = 12,
  height = 14
)
ss_na_frac <- aggregated_dt[, mean(
  is.na(`3ss`) | is.na(`3ssdown`) | is.na(`5ss`) | is.na(`5ssup`)
)]
stopifnot(ss_na_frac < 0.01)
```


```{r, join-pangolin}
# §4.13e-ext — Pangolin splice-site usage scores (written by pangolin_scores
# rule). Guarded: rule may not have finished yet.
if (file.exists("processed_data/pangolin_scores.csv")) {
  pangolin_raw <- fread("processed_data/pangolin_scores.csv")
  pangolin_raw[,
    site_class := fcase(
      site_type %in% c("donor", "upstream_donor", "alt_donor")            , "donor"    ,
      site_type %in% c("acceptor", "alt_acceptor", "downstream_acceptor") , "acceptor" ,
      default = NA_character_
    )
  ]
  pangolin_donor <- pangolin_raw[
    site_class == "donor",
    .(
      pangolin_donor_mean = mean(mean_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
      pangolin_donor_tissue_cv = mean(tissue_cv, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = event_id
  ]
  pangolin_acceptor <- pangolin_raw[
    site_class == "acceptor",
    .(
      pangolin_acceptor_mean = mean(mean_usage, na.rm = TRUE),
      pangolin_acceptor_tissue_cv = mean(tissue_cv, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = event_id
  ]

  id_map <- unique(event_annotations_dt[, .(event_id, ID)])
  pangolin_dt <- id_map[pangolin_donor, on = .(event_id)]
  pangolin_dt[
    pangolin_acceptor,
    on = .(event_id),
    c("pangolin_acceptor_mean", "pangolin_acceptor_tissue_cv") := .(
      i.pangolin_acceptor_mean,
      i.pangolin_acceptor_tissue_cv
    )
  ]

  aggregated_dt[
    pangolin_dt,
    on = .(ID),
    c(
      "pangolin_donor_mean",
      "pangolin_donor_tissue_cv",
      "pangolin_acceptor_mean",
      "pangolin_acceptor_tissue_cv"
    ) := .(
      i.pangolin_donor_mean,
      i.pangolin_donor_tissue_cv,
      i.pangolin_acceptor_mean,
      i.pangolin_acceptor_tissue_cv
    )
  ]

  cor_5ss_pangolin <- cor(
    aggregated_dt[!duplicated(ID), `5ss`],
    aggregated_dt[!duplicated(ID), pangolin_donor_mean],
    method = "spearman",
    use = "complete.obs"
  )
  cat(sprintf(
    "Spearman r(5ss, pangolin_donor_mean) = %.3f (must be > 0.2)\n",
    cor_5ss_pangolin
  ))
  stopifnot(cor_5ss_pangolin > 0.2)
} else {
  warning(
    "processed_data/pangolin_scores.csv not found — skipping Pangolin join (§4.13e-ext)"
  )
}
```
